ask: C11, no dependencies. raster.c: software rasterizer — barycentric triangle fill with a z-buffer, perspective-correct interpolation of UVs, simple Lambert shading, and a PPM writer. main renders a spinning cube's three visible faces to out.ppm. write the file.
prose:
raster.c is written. Build and run with:

```
cc -std=c11 -O2 -o raster raster.c -lm
./raster
```

That produces `out.ppm` — a 640x640 image of a cube at a fixed angle (Y=35°, X=22°) showing three faces: front, right, and top. Each face gets flat Lambert shading from a single directional light plus a 0.12 ambient floor, textured with a yellow/navy checkerboard via perspective-correct UV interpolation. Back-face culling happens in two places (screen-space winding test in the rasterizer, world-space dot product before that) so only the three visible faces draw.
